draft.title: Arcs and sectors
card: An arc is part of the edge of a circle. A sector is the slice of the circle between two radii and an arc. The angle θ at the centre must be in radians.
Arc length
l = rθ. The length is the radius times the angle in radians.
Sector area
A = ½r²θ. Square the radius, multiply by θ, then halve.
Example
A sector has r = 6 cm and θ = 2 radians. Arc length = 6 × 2 = 12 cm. Area = ½ × 6² × 2 = ½ × 36 × 2 = 36 cm².
draft.remember: With θ in radians: arc length is rθ, and sector area is ½r²θ.

a.q: A sector has radius 5 cm and angle 3 radians. What is its arc length?
a.why: Arc length l = rθ = 5 × 3 = 15 cm. The answer 37.5 comes from the area formula ½r²θ, which gives an area in cm², not a length.
a.clue: Use the radius times the angle.

b.q: Mia cuts a slice of pizza shaped as a sector with radius 10 cm and angle 0.8 radians. What is the area of the slice?
b.why: A = ½r²θ = ½ × 10² × 0.8 = ½ × 100 × 0.8 = 40 cm². Forgetting the ½ gives 80 cm². Using rθ gives 8, which is the arc length.
b.clue: Square the radius first, then halve.

check.summary: No problems found. The formulas, worked example, both answers (15 cm and 40 cm²) and the explanations of the wrong options all check out.

final.title: Arcs and sectors
card: An arc is part of the edge of a circle. A sector is the slice of the circle between two radii and an arc. The angle \(\theta\) at the centre must be in radians.
Arc length
\(l = r\theta\). The length is the radius times the angle in radians.
Sector area
\(A = \frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta\). Square the radius, multiply by \(\theta\), then halve.
Example
A sector has \(r = 6\) cm and \(\theta = 2\) radians. Arc length is \(6 \times 2 = 12\) cm. Area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6^{2} \times 2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 36 \times 2 = 36 \text{ cm}^{2}\).
final.remember: With \(\theta\) in radians: arc length is \(r\theta\), and sector area is \(\frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta\).

a.q: A sector has radius 5 cm and angle 3 radians. What is its arc length?
a.why: Arc length \(l = r\theta = 5 \times 3 = 15\) cm. The answer 37.5 comes from the area formula \(\frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta\), which gives an area in \(\text{cm}^{2}\), not a length.
a.clue: Use the radius times the angle.

b.q: Mia cuts a slice of pizza shaped as a sector with radius 10 cm and angle 0.8 radians. What is the area of the slice?
b.why: \(A = \frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta = \frac{1}{2} \times 10^{2} \times 0.8\), which is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 100 \times 0.8 = 40 \text{ cm}^{2}\). Forgetting the \(\frac{1}{2}\) gives \(80 \text{ cm}^{2}\). Using \(r\theta\) gives 8, which is the arc length.
b.clue: Square the radius first, then halve.
